title: The absolute Gabber modification and its four-stage construction
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be an integral Noetherian quasi-excellent separated fs log regular scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Quasi-excellence of a scheme means that every affine open has quasi-excellent coordinate ring; separated means its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is closed. Let a finite group $G$ act by log automorphisms, tamely and generically freely: geometric-point stabilizers have order invertible in their residue fields, and the action is free on a dense invariant open. Write $Z$ for the complement of the log triviality locus and $F$ for the complement of the largest free open.

There is a choice, simultaneously for these triples, of a finite normalized blowup tower $b:X^*\to X$, equivariant for $G$, projective in the projective-bundle sense, and an isomorphism over $X\setminus(Z\cup F)$. Normalized blowup means ordinary blowup followed by normalization in the common function field. The source is integral and fs log regular, with boundary $b^{-1}(Z\cup F)$ and a very tame action. Very tame means that each geometric inertia group acts trivially on the characteristic monoid and on $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X^*,\bar x}/I_{\bar x})$, where $I_{\bar x}$ is generated by nonunit log sections [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and its order is invertible at $\bar x$.

The tower can be chosen as the following four-stage procedure. The first stage is a $G$-equivariant saturated log blowup tower making the source regular. The second is the boundary-stratum blowup tower making the boundary strict normal crossings and $G$-strict, where $G$-strict means that distinct translates of any boundary component are disjoint. Both stages are saturated log blowup towers. Strict normal crossings means a reduced divisor on a regular scheme with regular distinct components whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have codimension $r$. The third is the finite $G$-equivariant permissible fixed-locus blowup procedure: repeatedly blow up the nonempty minimal fixed subschemes and their strict transforms, replacing the boundary by its strict transform together with the exceptional divisor. Permissible means the center is locally cut out by a subset of regular parameters in which the boundary is a product of distinct parameters. This stage makes inertia abelian and the action free outside the boundary. Locally its operations are the fixed-locus blowups of X 1.4--1.7. The fourth is the abelian-inertia rigidification construction of VIII 5.3.8--5.5.5: enlarge the boundary locally to a very tame strict normal crossings boundary, resolve its quotient by functorial saturated log blowups, pull back in fs log schemes, and retain only the inverse image of the original boundary. This construction is independent of the auxiliary enlarged boundary and is compatible with strict inertia-preserving morphisms, so the local fourth-stage modifications glue. Strict means the source log structure is pulled back from the target; inertia-preserving means an isomorphism on geometric stabilizers.

If $X$ is quasi-projective of finite type over an affine Noetherian scheme $B$, then $b$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective], and $X^*$ is quasi-projective of finite type over $B$. Quasi-projective means a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$.

source.place: VIII Theorem 1.1, 4.1.1--4.2.13, 5.3.8--5.5.5 and Theorem 5.6.1, pp.85,117--129; X 1.3--1.4, pp.139--141 (the operations used in the relative proof). Finite-projective-space refinement uses the ample base in the last paragraph.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8.
